content.title: Game Preview: Warriors vs. Brooklyn Nets - 3/25/26
content.text: March 24, 20269:24 AM PDTWARRIORS SEEK CONSECUTIVE WINS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE BUTLER III'S INJURYThe Warriors head home to Chase Center, where they’ll host the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. The Dubs are looking to stack wins in consecutive games for the first time since Jimmy Butler III’s injury on Jan. 19. Wednesday is Latino Heritage Night at Chase Center, presented by Modelo and the first 10,000 fans in attendance will receive an Al Horford bobblehead. LAST TIME OUTThe Warriors battled for a hard-fought overtime win, 137-131, over the Dallas Mavericks at American Airlines Arena on Monday. Moses Moody led the way with 23 points and three steals, Kristaps Porzingis added 22 points, seven rebounds and five assists and Brandin Podziemski chipped in with a 20-point 10-rebound double-double. Gary Payton II shot a perfect 8-for-8 from the field tallying 17 points. Mavericks' standout rookie Cooper Flagg led all players with 32 points and nine assists, Daniel Gafford also went 8-for-8 from the field for 20 points and Klay Thompson scored 15 points all from his five made 3-pointers. »Full StoryVideo Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 1:59Remaining Time 1:59Highlights: Warriors vs. Dallas Mavericks | 2/23/26PORZINGIS SHOWS PROMISE ON REUNION TOURTypically, a player returning to play against their former team, especially in that team’s building, stands out as a marquee matchup on the NBA calendar. For Kristaps Porzingis, who was just four games into his Warriors tenure, it was a staple of the latest road trip. During a six-game trip, the Warriors visited five of Porzingis’ former teams, including the New York Knicks, Washington Wizards, Boston Celtics, Atlanta Hawks and Dallas Mavericks. Porzingis played in three of those games, beginning in the nation’s capital. »Full StoryVideo Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 1:42Remaining Time 1:42Highlights: Kristaps Porzingis Scores 30 Points in Win Over Wizards | 3/16/26HOW THEY'RE TRENDING: Warriors: Gary Payton II set a new career-high for most made field goals in a game without a miss when he made all eight of his shots against the Dallas Mavericks on Monday. Payton became the first Warrior to make at least eight shots without a miss since Trayce Jackson-Davis went 9-for-9 against the New York Knicks on March 18 2024. Nets: The Nets enter Wednesday’s game on an eight-game losing streak, including two losses to the Portland Trail Blazers, who jumped ahead of the Warriors in the standings. Star forward Michael Porter Jr. has missed the last seven games and is expected to miss this one with a left hamstring strain. Brooklyn has the NBA’s third-worst record, 0.5 games ahead of the Washington Wizards and a game ahead of the Indiana Pacers. The first 10,000 fans in attendance for Thursday's game will receive a Warriors patch. HomeThu Apr 027:00 PM PDTTV: NBCSBARadio: 95.7 The GameWatchCOMPELLING NOTE: Warriors: Heading into the month of April, the Warriors are two losses away being unable to secure the seventh seed in the Western Conference and the opportunity to host both Play-In games. The Warriors know two of the three teams that will be joining them in the Play-In Tournament which include the Los Angeles Clippers and Portland Trail Blazers. If the Dubs can get the eighth or ninth seed, they will have the opportunity to host one of those two games, otherwise they’ll be on the road for both tournament games. Cavaliers: The Cavaliers are one of three teams with two top-25 scorers, with Donovan Mitchell (8th; 27.7 PPG) and James Harden (22nd; 23.7 PPG) combining to average 51.4 points per game. Cleveland’s duo joins the Denver Nuggets’ Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray and the Los Angeles Lakers’ Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Registration is now open for all summer camp sessions at gssportsacademy.com. Golden State Sports Academy will host two overnight camps at the Sephora Performance Center in Oakland this summer. The first session will run from July 3–6 featuring a planned appearance by Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski, and the second session will run from August 6–9 featuring planned appearances by Warriors guard Will Richard and forward Gui Santos. This marks the fifth consecutive year the team has hosted an overnight camp. The summer schedule will run from June 1 through August 9, which includes clinics at Chase Center in San Francisco and Kaiser Permanente Arena in Santa Cruz. General week-long camp sessions will focus on individual skill development, the importance of fundamentals, and the development of a healthy team attitude for youth ages seven and up of all skill levels and abilities. In addition to the general sessions, the summer schedule will also include two all-girl sessions and two Valkyries camps in Northern California locations beyond the Bay Area. For complete details on Golden State Basketball Camp and to register online, visit gssportsacademy.com or call (510) 986-5310. Earlier this year, Golden State Sports Academy announced its expanded collaboration with Shoot 360, launching three new Bay Area training locations in Spring 2026. Located within City Sports Clubs in Stonestown (San Francisco), Almaden (San Jose), and Newhall (San Jose), these facilities will offer athletes ages 8 and up access to professional-level performance tracking and data-driven coaching. For complete details on Golden State Shoot 360 memberships and to place a deposit online, visit gsshoot360.com or call (510) 986-5310.
